questions.q: The area of the region (in sq. units) enclosed by the curves $y=8 x^3-1, y=0, x=-1$ and $x=1$ is
questions.solution: Required area $\begin{aligned} & =\int_{-1}^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(1-8 x^3\right) d x+\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^1\left(8 x^3-1\right) d x \\ & =\left[x-2 x^4\right]_{-1}^{\frac{1}{2}}+\left[2 x^4-x\right]_{\frac{1}{2}}^1 \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8}\right)-(-1-2)+(2-1)-\left(\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{19}{4} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the region bounded by the circle $x^2+y^2=64$, positive $x$-axis and the line $y=\sqrt{3} x$ is
questions.solution:
$x^2+y^2=64 \Rightarrow y=\sqrt{3} x\begin{aligned} & y^2=3 x^2 \Rightarrow x= \pm 4 \\ & \therefore \quad y=\sqrt{48}\end{aligned}$
Area $=\int_0^4 y d x+\int_4^8 y_2 d x\begin{aligned} & =\int_0^4(\sqrt{3} x) d x+\int_4^8 \sqrt{64-x^2} d x \\ & =\left[\sqrt{3} \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4+\left[\frac{x}{2} \sqrt{64-x^2}+\frac{64}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{8}\right)\right]_4^8\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =8 \sqrt{3}+\left[32 \frac{\pi}{2}-2 \sqrt{48}-32 \cdot \frac{\pi}{6}\right] \\ & =16 \pi-\frac{16 \pi}{3}=\frac{32 \pi}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area lying in the first quadrant and bounded by the circle $x^2+y^2-4 x=0$, the parabola $y^2=x$ and the $X$-axis is $A$, then $6 A-9 \sqrt{3}=$
questions.solution:
Given curve $x^2+y^2-4 x=0 \Rightarrow(x-2)^2+y^2=4 \text{$ and } y^2=x intersecting point of circle and parabola is (0,0) and $(3, \sqrt{3})$ Required area
$A=\int_0^3 \sqrt{x} d x+\int_3^4 \sqrt{4-(x-2)^2} d x\begin{aligned} & A=\left[\frac{2}{3}(x)^{3 / 2}\right]_0^3+\left[\frac{x-2}{2} \sqrt{4-(x-2)^2}+2 \sin ^{-1} \frac{x-2}{2}\right]_3^4 \\ & A=2 \sqrt{3}+\left[\left(0+2 \sin ^{-1}(1)\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+2 \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\right] \\ & A=2 \sqrt{3}+\pi-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{2 \pi}{3} \\ & 6 A-9 \sqrt{3}=4 \pi\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq. units) enclosed by the curves $y=2 x-x^2$ and $y=x^2-2 x-6$ is
questions.solution:
Curves, $y=2 x-x^2 \Rightarrow y=x^2-2 x-6$ Intersecting points, $2 x-x^2=x^2-2 x-62 x^2-4 x-6=0$ or $x^2-2 x-3=0$ or $\quad(x-3)(x+1)=0$ or $x=-1, \quad x=3$ At $x=-1, y=2 \times(-1)-(-1)^2=-3$ At $x=3, y=-3$ So, both the curves are intersecting each other at points $(-1,-3)$ and $(3,-3)$
$\therefore$ Required area, $A=\int y_1 d x-\int y_2 d x=\int_{-1}^3\left(y_1-y_2\right) d x=\int_{-1}^3\left(2 x-x^2-x^2+2 x+6\right) d x=\int_{-1}^3\left(4 x-2 x^2+6\right) d x=\left[2 x^{-2}-\frac{2}{3} x^3+6 x\right]_{-1}^3=\left\{2(3)^2-\frac{2}{3}(3)^3+6(3)\right\}-\left\{2(-1)^2-\frac{2}{3}(-1)^3+6(-1)\right\}=18+\frac{10}{3}=\frac{64}{3}$ sq units

questions.q: The area (in square units) of the region enclosed between the parabola $y^2=2 x$ and the line $y=4 x-1$
questions.solution:
Given equation of parabola $y^2=2 x$ $\ldots(\mathrm{i})$ and equation of line $y=4 x-1$ $\ldots(\mathrm{ii})$ Intersecting points of Eqs. (i) and (ii) $\operatorname{are}\left(\frac{1}{8}, \frac{-1}{2}\right)$ and $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$
Required area $A O B$ $=\int_{-1 / 2}^1\left(\frac{y+1}{4}-\frac{y^2}{2}\right) d y$ $=\frac{1}{4} \int_{-1 / 2}^1(y+1) d y-\frac{1}{2} \int_{-1 / 2}^1 y^2 d y$ $=\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+y\right]_{-1 / 2}^1-\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1 / 2}^1$ $=\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(\frac{1}{2}+1\right)-\left(\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]-\frac{1}{6}\left[1-\left(-\frac{1}{8}\right)\right]$ $=\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{3}{2}+\frac{3}{8}\right]-\frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{9}{8}\right)=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{15}{8}-\frac{3}{16}$ $=\frac{15-6}{32}=\frac{9}{32}$ sq units

$|x|=2,|y|=2, x y \leq \frac{1}{2} \begin{aligned} \text{ Required area } & =2[2 \times 2]+2\left[\int_0^{1 / 4} 2 d x+\int_{1 / 4}^2 \frac{1}{2 x} d x\right] \\ & =8+2\left[2[x]_0^{1 / 4}+\frac{1}{2}[\log x]_{1 / 4}^2\right] \\ & =8+4\left[\frac{1}{4}-0\right]+\left[\log 2-\log \frac{1}{4}\right] \\ & =8+1+\log 2-\log \left(2^{-2}\right) \\ & =9+\log 2+2 \log 2=9+3 \log 2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the area of the region bounded by $y=\cos x$, $y=\sin x, x=\frac{\pi}{4}$ and $x=\pi$ is bisected by the line $x=a$, then $\sin \left(a+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=$
questions.solution: According to the question, $\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^a(\sin x-\cos x) d x=\int_a^\pi(\sin x-\cos x) d x\begin{aligned} {[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^a } & =[-\cos x-\sin x]_a^\pi \\ -\cos a & -\sin a+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=1+\cos a+\sin a \\ \sqrt{2}-1 & =2(\cos a+\sin a) \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2} & =\sin a+\cos a \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2 \sqrt{2}} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin a+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos a \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2 \sqrt{2}} & =\sin a \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{4}+\cos a \sin \frac{\pi}{4} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2 \sqrt{2}} & =\sin \left(a+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\end{aligned}$

$= 16\pia^{2} - 2{ \dfrac{2\sqrt{6a} ⋅ 2\sqrt{2}a\sqrt{a}}{3} + ( 8a^{2} ⋅ \dfrac{\pi}{2} - ( a ⋅ 2\sqrt{3}a + 8a^{2} ⋅ \dfrac{\pi}{6} ) ) }$

questions.q: The area enclosed by the curves $y=8 x-x^2$ and $8 x-4 y+11=0$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of curves are $$ \begin{aligned} & y=8 x-x^2 \\ & 8 x-4 y+11=0 \end{aligned} $$ Eq. (i) can be rewritten as $$ \begin{aligned} & y=-\left(x^2-2 \cdot 4 x+4^2-4^2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y=-\left[(x-4)^2-16\right] \\ & \Rightarrow \quad y-16=-(x-4)^2 \\ & \end{aligned} $$ $(x-4)^2=-(y-16)$, which represent a parabola open downward and having vertex at $(4,16)$. Clearly, Eq. (ii) represent a straight line passing through $\left(0, \frac{11}{4}\right)$ and $\left(-\frac{11}{8}, 0\right)$ Let us find the point of intersection of given curves, for this substitute the value of $y$ from Eq. (i) in Eq. (ii). $$ \begin{array}{rlrl} \Rightarrow & 8 x-4\left(8 x-x^2\right)+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 8 x-32 x+4 x^2+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 4 x^2-24 x+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 4 x^2-22 x-2 x+11 =0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x(2 x-11)-1(2 x-11) =0 \\ \Rightarrow & (2 x-1)(2 x-11) =0 \\ \Rightarrow & x =\frac{1}{2} \text{ or } \frac{11}{2} \end{array} $$ When $x=\frac{1}{2}$, then $y=\frac{15}{4}$ When $x=\frac{11}{2}$, then $y=\frac{55}{4} \quad$ [using Eq. (ii)] Now, required area $=$ Area of shaded region.
$$ =\int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}[y(\text{ parabola })-y(\text{ straight line })] d x $$ $$ \begin{aligned} & =\int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left[8 x-x^2-\left(\frac{8 x+11}{4}\right)\right] d x \\ & =\frac{1}{4} \int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left(32 x-4 x^2-8 x-11\right) d x \\ & =-\frac{1}{4} \int_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2}\left(4 x^2-24 x+11\right) d x \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left[\frac{4 x^3}{3}-24 \frac{x^2}{2}+11 x\right]_{1 / 2}^{11 / 2} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\left[\frac{4}{3} \cdot \frac{1331}{8}-12 \times \frac{121}{4}+\frac{121}{2}\right]-\left[\frac{1}{6}-3+\frac{11}{2}\right]\right\} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\frac{1331}{6}-363+\frac{121}{2}-\frac{1}{6}+3-\frac{11}{2}\right\} \\ & =\frac{-1}{4}\left\{\frac{1330}{6}-360+55\right\} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\frac{665}{3}-305\right\} \\ & =-\frac{1}{4}\left\{\frac{665-915}{3}\right\}=\frac{250}{4 \times 3}=\frac{125}{6} \text{ sq units } \end{aligned} $$

\Rightarrow & & \sqrt{x}\left(1-a^{3 / 2} x^{3 / 2}\right) & =0 \Rightarrow x=0, \frac{1}{a}\\
& \text{ When, }& x=0, y & =0 \\

& x=\frac{1}{a},y=\frac{1}{a}

$\begin{aligned}3 & =\int_0^{\frac{1}{a}} \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{a}}d x-\int_0^{\frac{1}{a}} a x² d x \\

\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow& 3 & =\frac{2}{3 \sqrt{a}}\left[\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^{3 / 2}\right]-\frac{a}{3}\left[\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)^3\right] \\
\Rightarrow & 3 & =\frac{2}{3 \sqrt{a}} \times \frac{1}{a \sqrt{a}}-\frac{a}{3} \times \frac{1}{a^3}\\

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq units) of the region bounded by $x=-1, x=2, y=x^2+1$ and $y=2 x-2$ is
questions.solution:
Given curve is $y=x^2+1 \Rightarrow x^2=y-1$ and line $\quad y=2 x-2$
The intersection point of curve and line is $\begin{aligned} & \qquad x^2=2 x-2-1 \\ & $\begin{array}{l}$\text{ Now, }$ \quad x^2-2 x+3=0 \\ $\text{ Hence, there$ is no point of intersection }\end{array}$ \\ & \therefore \text{ Required area }=\int_{-1}^2\left(y_2-y_1\right) d x \\ & \qquad=\int_{-1}^2\left[\left(x^2+1\right)-(2 x-2)\right] d x \\ & \qquad=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}+x\right]_{-1}^2-\left[x^2-2 x\right]_{-1}^2 \\ & =\left[\frac{8}{3}+2-\left(-\frac{1}{3}-1\right)\right]-[4-4-(1+2)] \\ & =\frac{14}{3}+\frac{4}{3}-[-3] \\ & =6+3=9\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq units) bounded by the curves $x=-2 y^2$ and $x=1-3 y^2$ is
questions.solution:
Given curves, $\text{$ and $} \quad \begin{aligned}& x=-2 y² \\
& x=1-3 y²
\end{aligned} On solving both curves, we get \begin{gathered}
-2 y²=1-3 y² \\
\Rightarrow \quad y=$\pm$1 \text{$ and }$ x=-2
\end{gathered} So, the intersection points are $(-2,1) and (-2,-1)$.
  \\ $\therefore$ Required area \begin{aligned}& =2 \int_0^1\left\{\left(1-3 y²\right)-\left(-2 y²\right)\right\} d y \\
& =2 \int_0^1\left(1-y²\right) d y \\
& =2\left( y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right)_0^1=2\left(1-\frac{1}{3}\right)\\
& =2 \times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3}
\end{aligned}$

$y^2=4 x$ and $x^2=4 y$ is

The intersection point is

 \begin{aligned}& =\int\left(y_2-y_1\right) d x \\ & =\int_0^4\left(\sqrt{4 x}-\frac{x^2}{4}\right)d x \\ & =\left[\frac{2 x^{3 / 2}}{3 / 2}-\frac{x^3}{12}\right]_0^4\\ & =\left[\frac{4}{3}(4)^{3 / 2}-\frac{(4)^3}{12}-(0-0)\right] \\ & =\left(\frac{32}{3}-\frac{64}{12}\right)=\frac{128-64}{12}\\ & =\frac{64}{12}=\frac{16}{3} \text{ sq units }\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given integration is $\int_0^4 \frac{d x}{1+x^2}$ and h=1.
By using Trapezoidal rule, $\begin{aligned} \int_0^4 f(x) d x & =\frac{h}{2}\left[\left(y_0+y_4\right)+2\left(y_1+y_2+y_3\right)\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(1+\frac{1}{17}\right)+2\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{10}\right)\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{18}{17}+2\left(\frac{5+2+1}{10}\right)\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{18}{17}+\frac{8}{5}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{90+136}{85}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{226}{85}\right)=\frac{113}{85}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area (in square units) of the region enclosed by the two circles $x^2+y^2=1$ and $(x-1)^2+y^2=1$ is
questions.solution:
Intersection point of two circles
$x^2+y^2=1$ $\ldots$ (i) $(x-1)^2+y^2=1$ $\ldots$ (ii) is given by $(x-1)^2+\left(1-x^2\right)=1$ $\Rightarrow \quad x^2+1-2 x-x^2=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{1}{2}$ From Eq. (i), $\frac{1}{4}+y^2=1$ $y^2=1-\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow y= \pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ Point $A\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ and $C\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ So, Area of region $O A B C O$ $=2 \times$ Area of region $O A B D O$ Area of $O A B D O$ $=$ Area of $O A D O+$ Area of $A B D A$ $=\int_0^{1 / 2} \sqrt{1-(x-1)^2} d x+\int_{1 / 2}^1 \sqrt{1-x^2} d x$ $=\left[\frac{1}{2} \cdot(x-1) \sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x-1}{1}\right)\right]_0^{1 / 2}$ $+\left[\frac{1}{2} x \sqrt{1-x^2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\right]_{1 / 2}^1$ $=\left[-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \cdot 0-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(-1)\right]$ $+\left[\frac{1}{2} \cdot 0+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(1)-\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]$ $=\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}\right)-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(1)$ $+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}(1)-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{8}-\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ $=\sin ^{-1}(1)-\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$ $=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$ $=\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)$ from Eq. (i), Area of region $O A B C O=2 \times\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)$ $=\left(\frac{2 \pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$

questions.q: The area enclosed (in square units) by the curve $y = {x}^{4} - {x}^{2}$, the $x$-axis and the vertical lines passing through the two minimum points of the curve is
questions.solution:
Given that $y = {x}^{4} - {x}^{2}$

For minimum points of curve:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2}\right) = 0$

$4{x}^{3} - 2x = 0$

$2x\left(2{x}^{2} - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2x = 0$ or $2{x}^{2} - 1 = 0$

$x = 0$ or $x = \dfrac{\pm 1}{\sqrt{2}}$

So $f$ is minimum at $\dfrac{\pm 1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The area $= \left|{∫}_{\dfrac{- 1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2}\right)dx\right|$

$= \left|2{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left({x}^{4} - {x}^{2}\right)dx\right|\left[∵ f\left(x\right)\text{is even function}\right]$

$= \left|2\left[\dfrac{{x}^{5}}{5} - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right]\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} 0\right|$

$= \left|2\left({\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{5} \cdot \dfrac{1}{5} - {\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}^{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|$

$= \left|2\left(\dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\right|$

$= \left|\dfrac{3 - 10}{30\sqrt{2}}\right|$

$∴$ Area $= \dfrac{7}{30\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curves $y=9 x^2$ and $y=5 x^2+4$ (in sq units) is
questions.solution:
Intersecting point of $y=9 x^2 and y=5 x^2+4$ is given by
 $\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow \quad 4 x²=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x²=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x= \pm1 \\
& \therefore \quad y=9( \pm1)^2=9 \\
&
\end{aligned} Hence, intersecting points are $( \pm 1,9)$. \begin{aligned}
\therefore\text{ Required area }& =2 \int_0^1\left[\left(5 x²+4\right)-\left(9 x²\right)\right] d x \\
& =2 \int_0^1\left(4-4 x²\right) d x \\
& =2\left[4 x-\frac{4 x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 \\
& =2\left(4-\frac{4}{3}\right)-(0-0)=2 \times \frac{8}{3}\\
& =\frac{16}{3} \text{ sq units }
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:

Point of intersections are (1,1) and $(1,-1) \begin{aligned} & \therefore \text{ Required area }=2 \int_0^1\left(x_2-x_1\right) d y \\ & =2 \int_0^1\left[\left(3-2 y^2\right)-y^2\right] d y=2\left[\left(3 y-\frac{3 y^3}{3}\right)\right]_0^1 \\ & =2[3-1]=4\end{aligned}$
